mainTopic: The power and rewards of צדקה, and the danger of ignoring the poor
overview: The גמרא finishes showing, from a פסוק in משלי, that someone who regularly gives צדקה merits children who are wise, wealthy, and masters of אגדה. A ברייתא then brings רבי מאיר's answer to a classic challenge: if God loves the poor, why doesn't He feed them? He lets us feed them so our צדקה saves us from גיהנום. טורנוסרופוס and רבי עקיבא debate this with competing parables about a king's slave and a king's son, and רבי עקיבא closes with a פסוק showing that charity is God's will even in hard times. רבי יהודה ברבי שלום teaches that a person's losses are fixed on ראש השנה, and the story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's nephews shows this in action. The story of רב פפא's near-fall leads to a ברייתא that compares ignoring the poor to עבודה זרה. A string of teachings then praises צדקה: it brings peace with ה׳, brings the גאולה closer, saves from death, earns a view of the שכינה, and counts as a loan to ה׳. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן explaining why two פסוקים say צדקה saves from death. One is about גיהנום and one is about an unusual death. The question of which צדקה saves from an unusual death is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the source for wisdom, and the source for wealth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the proof for 'masters of wisdom' ("יִמְצָא חַיִּים") and shows that 'masters of wealth' comes from the word "צְדָקָה".
steps.simpleTranslation: "...finds life" (this phrase is the source for masters of wisdom). Masters of wealth: as it is written, "charity."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of proving that a person who gives צדקה will have special children. Here it finishes the proof for wise children and gives the proof for wealthy children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base פסוק is משלי 21:21: one who pursues צדקה 'will find life, צדקה, and honor.' Each of the three rewards hints to one kind of child. 'Life' points to wisdom, and 'צדקה' points to wealth, since only a wealthy person has money to give צדקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of wealth, people with money

phrases.english: "finds life."
phrases.notes: The same words appear about wisdom in משלי 8:35: "he who finds Me finds life."

phrases.english: Masters of wealth —
as it is written: "charity."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, משלי 21:21. He will 'find צדקה,' meaning he will have money to give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי עוֹשֶׁר דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof begun earlier on the daf for רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement about the children of someone who gives צדקה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that one who gives צדקה merits wise and wealthy children

steps.title: Source for masters of אגדה, through the word 'honor'
steps.stepSummary: Masters of אגדה are learned from the word "וְכָבוֹד", which is linked to the פסוק "כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ".
steps.simpleTranslation: Masters of אגדה: as it is written, "and honor." It says 'honor' here, and it says 'honor' there: "The wise shall inherit honor."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third kind of child, masters of אגדה, from the word 'honor' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself, 'honor' doesn't obviously mean אגדה. So the גמרא links it to another פסוק where 'honor' goes to the wise. Since 'honor' is tied to wise people, and the other two rewards are already used up, the honor here points to wise teachers of אגדה, who win people's hearts.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of אגדה, the non-legal teachings of Torah
It is written here... and it is written there: linking two פסוקים by a shared word
Learning one פסוק from another through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: Regularly giving צדקה is rewarded with three kinds of children: wise (חיים), wealthy (צדקה), and masters of אגדה (כבוד).

phrases.english: Masters of aggadah — as it is written: "and honor."
It is written here: "and honor,"
and it is written there:
"The wise shall inherit honor."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:35

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא וְכָבוֹד וּכְתִיב הָתָם כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים יִנְחָלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part proof by explaining the last word of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that one who gives צדקה merits children who are masters of אגדה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'honor' in משלי 21:21, linked to משלי 3:35

steps.title: רבי מאיר: why God leaves the poor for us to support
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: an opponent may ask why God, who loves the poor, doesn't feed them. Answer: so that we are saved from גיהנום through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר used to say, an opponent may argue with you and say: If your God loves the poor, why doesn't He support them? Tell him: So that through them we will be saved from the judgment of גיהנום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. רבי מאיר raises a challenge a non-believer might make about the poor and gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge: if God really cared about the poor, He could easily feed them, so why does He leave them hungry? רבי מאיר's answer: God lets us be His helpers in feeding them. Our צדקה earns us merit that saves us from punishment in גיהנום.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
An opponent, one who argues against you

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a basic reason behind צדקה: the poor are not forgotten by God. Giving to them is a chance for us to earn merit.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Meir would say,
an opponent may argue back at you
and say to you:
If your God loves the poor,
why does He not support them?
Say to him:
So that we will be saved through them
phrases.notes: 'Through them' means through the צדקה we give them.

phrases.english: from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new idea about צדקה, connected to the earlier praise of giving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God leaves the poor for us to support so that our צדקה saves us from גיהנום.

steps.title: טורנוסרופוס asks רבי עקיבא the same question
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says this exact question was once asked by טורנוסרופוס to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the question that טורנוסרופוס the wicked asked רבי עקיבא: If your God loves the poor, why doesn't He support them?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us this was a real question, once asked of רבי עקיבא. It is setting up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is word for word the same as in רבי מאיר's teaching. This shows that רבי מאיר's 'opponent' was not just imaginary.

keyTerms.meaning: טורנוסרופוס the wicked, a non-Jew who argued with רבי עקיבא

phrases.english: And this is the question that
Turnus Rufus the wicked asked Rabbi Akiva:
If your God loves the poor,
why does He not support them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ שְׁאֵלָה שָׁאַל טוֹרָנוּסְרוּפוּס הָרָשָׁע אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real-life case of the question רבי מאיר described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why God, who loves the poor, does not provide for them Himself

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gives the same answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answered that God leaves the poor for us so we can be saved from גיהנום through them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: So that through them we will be saved from the judgment of גיהנום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers טורנוסרופוס with the same answer רבי מאיר taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Supporting the poor is a מצוה that brings merit. By leaving the job to us, God gives us a way to be saved.

keyTerms.meaning: גיהנום, the place of punishment after death

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּדֵי שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל אָנוּ בָּהֶן
phrases.english: He said to him: So that we will be saved through them
from the judgment of Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל אָנוּ בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of טורנוסרופוס.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God lets us support the poor so that our צדקה saves us from גיהנום.

steps.title: טורנוסרופוס: giving charity makes God angry, like feeding a punished slave
steps.stepSummary: טורנוסרופוס argues the opposite: צדקה should bring punishment, like someone who feeds a slave the king has jailed and ordered starved. Jews are called God's slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On the contrary, this is what makes you liable for גיהנום! I'll give you a parable. A human king got angry at his slave, put him in prison, and ordered that no one feed him or give him drink. Someone went and fed him and gave him drink. When the king hears, won't he be angry at that person? And you are called slaves, as it says: "For the children of Israel are slaves to Me."
steps.whatsHappening: טורנוסרופוס attacks רבי עקיבא's answer. He claims that giving צדקה actually goes against God's will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: if God made someone poor, God wants him to suffer, like a king punishing a slave. Helping the poor person goes against the king's order, so it should make God angry, not reward you. He proves Jews are slaves from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A king of flesh and blood, a human king

phrases.english: He said to him: On the contrary,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: this is what makes you liable for Gehinnom!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the צדקה itself.

phrases.english: I will give you a parable,
what is this comparable to?

phrases.aramaic: לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁכָּעַס עַל עַבְדּוֹ,
phrases.english: To a king of flesh and blood who was angry at his slave,
and locked him in prison,
and gave orders about him
that he not be fed and not be given to drink.
And one person went
and fed him and gave him drink.
When the king heard,
would he not be angry at him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person who fed the slave.

phrases.english: And you are called slaves,
as it is stated: "For the children of Israel are slaves to Me"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:55

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ אַדְּרַבָּה זוֹ שֶׁמְּחַיַּיבְתָּן לְגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that צדקה saves from גיהנום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If God made someone poor as a punishment, helping him defies the King's order, just as feeding a king's jailed slave would anger the king. Since Jews are called God's slaves, צדקה should bring punishment, not reward.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: we are God's children, and feeding a jailed son earns a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with a better parable: a king who jails his son would reward someone who fed him. Jews are called God's children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: I'll give you a parable. A human king got angry at his son, put him in prison, and ordered that no one feed him or give him drink. Someone went and fed him and gave him drink. When the king hears, won't he send that person a gift? And we are called sons, as it says: "You are sons of ה׳ your God."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends his answer by changing the parable from a slave to a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king may punish his son in anger, but deep down he loves him. Once his anger cools, he is grateful to whoever kept his son alive. Since the פסוק calls Jews God's children, helping a poor Jew is something God rewards.
steps.confusionAlert: Both parables are almost word for word the same. The only real difference is slave vs. son, and that one change flips anger into a gift.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on how God relates to us: as slaves (helping goes against Him) or as children (helping pleases Him). רבי עקיבא says we are children, so צדקה is rewarded. טורנוסרופוס pushes back in step 8, and רבי עקיבא answers in step 9.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
I will give you a parable:
what is this comparable to?

phrases.aramaic: לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁכָּעַס עַל בְּנוֹ
phrases.english: To a king of flesh and blood who was angry at his son
and locked him in prison,
and gave orders about him
that he not be fed and not be given to drink.
And one person went
and fed him and gave him drink.
When the king heard,
would he not send him a gift?!
And we are called sons,
as it is written: "You are sons of the Lord your God"!
phrases.notes: דברים 14:1

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers טורנוסרופוס's parable with a parallel parable that reaches the opposite result.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-parable that changes the key detail (son instead of slave)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Jews are God's slaves, so helping the poor goes against His decree and brings anger.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jews are God's children, so even when He punishes, He is grateful to whoever helps, and צדקה is rewarded.

steps.title: טורנוסרופוס: Right Now You Are Slaves, Not Sons
steps.stepSummary: טורנוסרופוס agrees that Jews are sometimes called sons, but says that only applies when they do God's will. Since they don't do it now, they count as slaves, and his parable is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are called both sons and slaves. When you do God's will, you are called sons. When you don't do God's will, you are called slaves. And right now you are not doing God's will!
steps.whatsHappening: טורנוסרופוס strikes back against רבי עקיבא's parable of the king's son. He says the 'son' title depends on behavior, and right now the Jews are failing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא had said the Jews are God's children, so feeding them earns a reward. טורנוסרופוס accepts that both titles appear, but says which one applies depends on whether they do רצונו של מקום. Since they don't right now, his first parable (the slave the king wants starved) is back in force.

keyTerms.meaning: The will of God (מָקוֹם, 'the Place,' is a name for God)

phrases.english: He said to him: You are called sons
phrases.notes: 'He' here is טורנוסרופוס, answering רבי עקיבא's parable about the king's son.

phrases.english: and you are called slaves.

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאַתֶּם עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: When you do the will of the Omnipresent,
you are called sons.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאֵין אַתֶּם עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
phrases.english: And when you do not do the will of the Omnipresent,
you are called slaves.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַכְשָׁיו אֵין אַתֶּם עוֹשִׂים רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם!
phrases.english: And now you are not doing the will of the Omnipresent!
phrases.notes: He leaves the conclusion unsaid: so right now you are slaves, and my parable fits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אַתֶּם קְרוּיִם בָּנִים וּקְרוּיִן עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's parable of the son from step 7 by limiting when the 'son' title applies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that Jews are God's children, so feeding them earns a reward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'son' title depends on doing God's will. Right now Jews don't, so they are slaves, and feeding them goes against the King's wishes.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: The פסוק Commands צדקה Even in Hard Times
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא quotes ישעיהו: 'Share your bread with the hungry, and bring the cast-out poor into your house.' The cast-out poor exist in times like now, and that is exactly when the פסוק commands us to feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The פסוק says, 'Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the cast-out poor into your house?' When are there 'cast-out poor'? Now, in these hard times. And right then the פסוק says, 'share your bread with the hungry.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers טורנוסרופוס with a פסוק. Even in a time when the Jewish people are suffering and 'cast out,' God still commands feeding the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טורנוסרופוס claimed God wants the poor left hungry in times like now. רבי עקיבא points out that the same פסוק that talks about our hard times also commands us to feed the hungry. So even now, giving צדקה is God's will, not against it.

keyTerms.meaning: Share (literally 'break') your bread with the hungry
Poor people who are cast out, homeless and suffering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's final point: the פסוק commands charity specifically in times of hardship, so giving צדקה is always what God wants, even when the Jewish people are not at their best.

phrases.english: He said to him: Behold, it says:
phrases.notes: Now 'he' is רבי עקיבא, and 'it' is the פסוק.

phrases.english: "Is it not to share your bread with the hungry,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: and you shall bring the cast-out poor into your house."
When is it "bring the cast-out poor into your house"?
Nowadays,
and it says: "Is it not to share your bread with the hungry."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers טורנוסרופוס's challenge from step 8 using a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that God commands charity even in the 'slave' situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a time when Jews don't do God's will, feeding the poor goes against what God wants.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק itself commands feeding the hungry in exactly such hard times, so צדקה is always God's will.

steps.title: Yearly Losses Are Fixed on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ברבי שלום teaches that just as a person's income is set on ראש השנה, so are his losses. If he merits, the loss goes to צדקה. If not, it is taken from him by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה ברבי שלום taught: Just as a person's income is set for him from ראש השנה, so too his losses are set for him from ראש השנה. If he merits, 'share your bread with the hungry.' If he does not merit, 'bring the cast-out poor into your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about the same פסוק: the money a person will lose this year is already decided. The only question is whether it goes to צדקה or is lost in an unpleasant way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ברבי שלום reads the two halves of the פסוק as two possible paths for the same set amount of loss. If he merits, he gives it away willingly to the hungry. If he doesn't, unwanted people come into his house and use up his money against his will.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why giving צדקה never truly makes a person poorer: the loss was already decreed, and צדקה turns it into a מצוה instead of a forced loss.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shalom taught:
Just as a person's livelihood
is fixed for him from ראש השנה,
so too a person's losses
are fixed for him from ראש השנה.
If he merits: "Is it not to share your bread with the hungry."
phrases.notes: The money he is going to lose ends up going to the poor as צדקה.

phrases.english: If he does not merit: "And you shall bring the cast-out poor into your house."
phrases.notes: Here the same words are read as unwanted guests he is forced to take in and feed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 9 to teach a new idea about fixed yearly losses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's losses are set on ראש השנה. Merit decides whether they go to צדקה or are taken by force.

steps.title: The Story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's Nephews
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי dreamed his nephews would lose 700 דינרים that year. He pushed them to give צדקה, and they gave all but 17. On ערב יום כיפור, the government took exactly those 17.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of the nephews of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He saw in a dream that they were going to lose 700 דינרים. He pressured them and took money from them for צדקה. They had 17 דינרים left. When ערב יום כיפור came, the government sent people and took them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that shows רבי יהודה ברבי שלום's teaching in real life. The decreed loss of 700 was filled partly by צדקה and the rest by the government.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 700 דינרים loss was fixed, just as the teaching said. Whatever the nephews gave to צדקה counted toward it ('if he merits'). The 17 they didn't give were taken by force ('if he does not merit').

keyTerms.meaning: The government, literally 'the house of Caesar'

phrases.english: Like this story of the sons of the sister
of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.
He saw about them in a dream
that they were going to lose seven hundred dinars.
He pressured them and took from them for charity,
and seventeen dinars remained with them.
When the eve of Yom Kippur arrived,
the government sent and took them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דִּבְנֵי אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the teaching of step 10 with a story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה ברבי שלום's teaching that yearly losses are fixed and can go to צדקה or be taken by force
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's nephews, who lost exactly 700 דינרים: 683 to צדקה and 17 to the government

steps.title: The Nephews Ask Why He Kept the Dream Secret
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reassures his nephews that nothing more will be taken, since the 17 were all that was left. He reveals the dream, and they ask why he didn't tell them so they could give the rest too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said to them: Don't be afraid. They took the 17 דינרים you had left. They said to him: How do you know? He said: I saw a dream about you. They said: So why didn't you tell us, so we would have given them?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי calms his nephews and reveals his dream. They then ask why he hid it from them, which sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nephews worry the government will take even more. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי knows the loss is complete, because only the decreed amount could be taken. Their question makes sense: had they known, they could have given the last 17 to צדקה too.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said to them:
Do not be afraid,
the seventeen dinars you had, they took from you.
They said to him: How do you know?
He said to them: I saw a dream about you.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְאַמַּאי לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן [דְּנִיתְּבִינְהוּ]?
phrases.english: They said to him: And why did you not tell us, so that we would give them?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets; it spells out that they would have given the 17 to צדקה too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְאַמַּאי לָא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 11 and raises the question of why the dream was hidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי didn't reveal the dream, which would have let them give all 700 to צדקה

steps.title: So You Would Do the מצוה for Its Own Sake
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains that he kept quiet so his nephews would give צדקה purely as a מצוה, not just to beat a decreed loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I said to myself, better that you do the מצוה for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers his nephews' question. He wanted their giving to be a pure מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they had known about the decreed loss, their צדקה would have been a smart money move, since the money was going to be lost anyway. By keeping quiet, he made sure they gave for the sake of the מצוה itself. He was willing to let them lose 17 דינרים so the 683 they gave would be a complete מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה done for its own sake, not for personal gain

steps.whatToRemember: Losses are fixed on ראש השנה, and צדקה can take the place of a forced loss. But the ideal is still to give צדקה לשמה, purely as a מצוה, which is why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי kept his dream secret.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the reason to give צדקה is to avoid losses. The story makes the opposite point: the best giving is giving that has nothing to do with gaining or saving money.

phrases.english: He said to them: I said (to myself),
so that you would do the מצוה for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אָמֵינָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתַעְבְּדוּ מִצְוָה לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the nephews' question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He hid the dream so their צדקה would be a מצוה לשמה and not a way to avoid a decreed loss.

steps.title: רב פפא nearly falls and wonders why
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא slips on a ladder and almost falls. He asks if he deserves a punishment like those who break שבת or worship עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא was climbing a ladder. His foot slipped and he almost fell. He said: Now, am I liable like people who break שבת and worship idols?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רב פפא almost falls and wonders what sin he did to deserve it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling from a height is close to the death penalty of סקילה (stoning), which is given for breaking שבת and for עבודה זרה. רב פפא is puzzled, because he knows he did not commit such serious sins. He asks the question about himself, but in an indirect, polite way.
steps.confusionAlert: "The one who hates us" does not mean an enemy. It is a polite way for רב פפא to talk about himself without saying something bad about himself directly.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa was climbing up a ladder,
his foot slipped and he was about to fall.
He said: Now, is it so?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Either way, it opens a surprised question.

phrases.english: Is the one who hates us liable
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying "me." He doesn't want to say something harsh about himself directly.

phrases.english: like those who break Shabbos and those who worship idols?
phrases.notes: Both of these sins get סקילה, a death that comes from a fall, so his near-fall reminded him of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא הֲוָה סָלֵיק בְּדַרְגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that continues the larger theme of צדקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin could have caused רב פפא to almost suffer a punishment like סקילה?

steps.title: Perhaps you ignored a poor person
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב מדפתי suggests that רב פפא once turned away a poor person who came to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב מדפתי said to רב פפא: Maybe a poor person came to you and you did not support him.
steps.whatsHappening: חייא בר רב מדפתי answers רב פפא's question. He suggests the sin was not supporting a poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer connects ignoring the poor to the serious sins רב פפא mentioned. That sounds surprising, so the next step brings a ברייתא to show that ignoring צדקה really is compared to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: You supported him, you provided for him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Chiya bar Rav from Difti said to Rav Pappa:
Perhaps a poor person came to you
and you did not support him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא עָנִי בָּא לְיָדְךָ וְלֹא פִּרְנַסְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The near-punishment may have come because רב פפא once failed to support a poor person.

steps.title: Ignoring צדקה is like idol worship
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהושע בן קרחה teaches that one who turns away from צדקה is like one who worships עבודה זרה, learned from the shared word בליעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: Anyone who turns his eyes away from charity is as if he worships idols. It says here: 'Beware that there be no base thought in your heart,' and it says there: 'Base men went out.' Just as there it is about idol worship, so too here it is like idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that ignoring a poor person is as serious as the sins רב פפא mentioned. This explains why his near-fall could come from that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a גזירה שוה, using the same word in two פסוקים. The פסוק about refusing to lend to the poor uses the word בליעל, and so does the פסוק about people who lead a city to עבודה זרה. Because the word is the same, the sin of ignoring the poor is compared to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who turns his eyes away, ignores
It is written here, and it is written there. This is the setup for comparing two פסוקים
Just as there, so too here

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז"ל view ignoring a poor person. It is not just a missed מצוה. It is compared to one of the worst sins.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
Anyone who turns his eyes away from charity
is as if he worships idols.
It is written here: "Beware

phrases.aramaic: פֶּן יִהְיֶה דָבָר עִם לְבָבְךָ בְּלִיַּעַל״,
phrases.english: lest there be a base thought in your heart,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9. This פסוק is about refusing to help a poor brother.

phrases.english: and it is written there: "Base men have gone out."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:14

phrases.english: Just as there it is idol worship,
so too here it is like idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports חייא בר רב's answer by showing that ignoring צדקה is compared to עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaObject: That ignoring a poor person can deserve a punishment like the one given for עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהושע בן קרחה, using the shared word בליעל in דברים 15:9 and דברים 13:14.

steps.title: צדקה and חסד make peace with ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי teaches that צדקה and חסד bring great peace and act as defense lawyers between ישראל and ה׳, proven from ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said: All the charity and kindness that Jews do in this world bring great peace and are great defenders between ישראל and their Father in Heaven. As it says: 'So says ה׳: Do not enter a house of mourning, do not go to lament or bemoan them, for I have taken away My peace from this people... the kindness and the mercy.' Kindness means acts of kindness. Mercy means charity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא praising צדקה. This one shows the good side: צדקה and חסד bring peace between ישראל and ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק‎, ה׳ says He took away His peace, and together with it the חסד and the רחמים. This shows that peace and these good deeds go together. The ברייתא explains that חסד means גמילות חסדים and רחמים means צדקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Defense lawyers, advocates who speak up for someone
Acts of kindness, helping others with your body and effort

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
All charity and kindness
that the Jewish people do in this world
are great peace and great defenders
between Israel and their Father in Heaven,
as it is said: "So says ה׳:
Do not enter a house of mourning,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 16:5

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל תֵּלֵךְ לִסְפּוֹד וְאַל תָּנֹד לָהֶם,
phrases.english: do not go to lament, and do not bemoan them,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָסַפְתִּי אֶת שְׁלוֹמִי מֵאֵת הָעָם הַזֶּה וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: for I have taken away My peace from this people, etc.,
the kindness and the mercy."
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: "Kindness": this is acts of kindness.
"Mercy": this is charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the danger of ignoring צדקה to the reward of giving it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה and חסד bring great peace and act as defenders between ישראל and ה׳.

steps.title: צדקה brings the גאולה closer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה teaches that צדקה is great because it brings the גאולה closer, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says: Charity is great, because it brings the redemption closer. As it says: 'So says ה׳: Keep justice and do charity, for My salvation is near to come and My righteousness to be revealed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא in praise of צדקה. This one is about the whole nation: צדקה brings the גאולה closer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "do צדקה" right next to "My salvation is near." רבי יהודה reads this as cause and effect: when we give צדקה‎, ה׳ brings the ישועה closer.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Great is charity, because it brings the redemption closer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּה אָמַר ה׳, שִׁמְרוּ מִשְׁפָּט וַעֲשׂוּ צְדָקָה,
phrases.english: as it is said: "So says ה׳: Keep justice and do charity,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 56:1

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קְרוֹבָה יְשׁוּעָתִי לָבֹא וְצִדְקָתִי לְהִגָּלוֹת״.
phrases.english: for My salvation is near to come, and My righteousness to be revealed."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another praise of צדקה. After peace with ה׳ in step 17, now the גאולה.

steps.title: Ten strong things, and צדקה beats death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה lists ten strong things, each beaten by the next. Death is the strongest of all, but צדקה saves from death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to say: Ten strong things were created in the world. A mountain is strong, but iron cuts it. Iron is strong, but fire melts it. Fire is strong, but water puts it out. Water is strong, but clouds carry it. Clouds are strong, but wind scatters them. Wind is strong, but the body withstands it. The body is strong, but fear breaks it. Fear is strong, but wine chases it away. Wine is strong, but sleep sobers it off. And death is stronger than all of them, but charity saves from death, as it is written: 'And charity saves from death.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה builds a chain of strong things, where each one is beaten by the next. The chain ends with death, the strongest, and then shows that צדקה beats even death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every link in the chain shows that even something very strong has something stronger than it. Death seems to be the final, unbeatable power. The פסוק in משלי teaches that צדקה is stronger still, because it saves a person from death.

keyTerms.meaning: Chases it away, makes it fade
Sobers it off, wears it away

steps.whatToRemember: This section is all about the power of צדקה. Ignoring the poor is compared to עבודה זרה. Giving brings peace with ה׳, brings the גאולה closer, and is stronger than death itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to רב פפא's near-fall: just as ignoring the poor can bring a person close to death, giving צדקה can save him from death.

phrases.english: He used to say:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהודה from the step before.

phrases.english: Ten strong things were created in the world:
A mountain is strong, but iron cuts it.
Iron is strong, but fire melts it.
Fire is strong, but water puts it out.
Water is strong, but clouds carry it.
Clouds are strong, but wind scatters them.
Wind is strong, but the body withstands it.
The body is strong, but fear breaks it.
Fear is strong, but wine chases it away.
Wine is strong, but sleep wears it off.
And death is stronger than all of them,
and charity saves from death,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And charity saves from death."
phrases.notes: משלי 10:2

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר, עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים קָשִׁים נִבְרְאוּ בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same רבי יהודה, raising the praise of צדקה to its highest point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death is the strongest force in the world, but צדקה saves from death.

steps.title: A gift to a king versus a coin to a poor person
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי teaches that a human king may not accept your gift or see you, but ה׳ lets even a person who gives a פרוטה receive the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי taught: Come and see how different ה׳ is from people. When a person brings a big gift to a king, maybe the king will take it and maybe he won't. Even if he takes it, maybe the person will get to see the king and maybe he won't. ה׳ is not like that. A person gives just a פרוטה to a poor person and he gets to greet the שכינה, as the פסוק says: 'I, through צדק, will see Your face.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי compares a big gift to a human king with a tiny gift to a poor person. He shows that the tiny gift to the poor earns much more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a human king, there are two doubts: will he accept the gift, and even if he does, will you see him? With ה׳, there is no doubt at all, and even a tiny coin is enough. The proof is the word בצדק in the פסוק, which is read as 'through צדקה.'

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a lesson from the פסוקים
The way of flesh and blood, how human beings act
The face of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai expounded:
Come and see,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא – מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם;
phrases.english: that the way of flesh and blood is not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He;
the way of flesh and blood:
a person brings a big gift to the king,
it is uncertain whether they will accept it from him,
or whether they will not accept it from him;
and even if you say that they do accept it from him,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they help the second doubt flow from the first.

phrases.english: it is uncertain whether he will see the king's face,
or whether he will not see the king's face.
But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not like that:
a person gives a פרוטה to a poor person,
and he merits to receive the face of the שכינה,
as it says: 'I, through righteousness, will see Your face,
I will be satisfied, when I awake, with Your image.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 17:15. The word בצדק is being read as 'through צדקה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching in the chain of praises of צדקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a פרוטה given to the poor earns the giver the presence of the שכינה, unlike a gift to a human king.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר gives צדקה before praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר would give a פרוטה to a poor person and then pray, basing this on the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר would give a פרוטה to a poor person and only then pray. He explained: because it says, 'I, through צדק, will see Your face.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רבי אלעזר put this פסוק into practice. Before he prayed, he gave צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayer is like standing before ה׳'s face. Since the פסוק says we see ה׳'s face 'through צדקה,' רבי אלעזר gave צדקה first so he would be worthy to stand before ה׳ in prayer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar would give a פרוטה to a poor person,
and then he would pray.
He said: because it is written:
'I, through righteousness, will see Your face.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר יָהֵיב פְּרוּטָה לְעָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical application of the פסוק quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving צדקה before prayer, since seeing ה׳'s face comes through צדקה.

steps.title: What does the end of the פסוק mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the second half of the פסוק: 'I will be satisfied, when I awake, with Your image.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'I will be satisfied, when I awake, with Your image' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The first half of the פסוק was explained. Now the גמרא asks what the second half means, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'when I awake' are unclear: who is awake, and why does that bring a reward? The question invites an explanation of this phrase.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'I will be satisfied, when I awake, with Your image'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the first half of the פסוק to its second half.

steps.title: Scholars who stay awake are rewarded with the light of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the פסוק is about תלמידי חכמים who give up sleep to learn, and are rewarded in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: These are תלמידי חכמים who push sleep away from their eyes in this world to learn, and ה׳ fills them with the shine of the שכינה in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. 'When I awake' means people who stay awake to learn תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בהקיץ' is read as staying awake instead of sleeping. Their reward matches what they gave up: they lost sleep, and they will be 'satisfied' with the light of the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The shine, radiance of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
These are Torah scholars
who push sleep away from their eyes in this world,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, satisfies them
with the shine of the שכינה in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase refers to תלמידי חכמים who stay awake to learn and are rewarded with the light of the שכינה in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Giving to the poor is lending to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that one who gives to the poor lends to ה׳, and if the פסוק did not say so, we could never say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What does the פסוק mean, 'One who is kind to the poor lends to ה׳'? If the פסוק did not write it, we could not say it, because it is as if, so to speak, 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן points out how amazing the פסוק is: giving to the poor is like giving ה׳ a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק says a borrower is like a servant to the lender. So if ה׳ is the 'borrower,' it is as if ה׳ owes the giver, which we would never dare say on our own. Only because the פסוק says it may we say it, showing how great צדקה is.

keyTerms.meaning: Is kind to a poor person
So to speak, as if it were possible

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'One who is kind to the poor lends to ה׳'?
phrases.notes: משלי 19:17

phrases.english: If the verse were not written,
it would be impossible to say it,
since, so to speak, 'the borrower is a servant to the lender.'
phrases.notes: משלי 22:7. He means it would sound like ה׳ is in the giver's debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״מַלְוֵה ה׳ חוֹנֵן דַּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another praise of giving to the poor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who gives to the poor is considered to have lent to ה׳.

steps.title: Why do two פסוקים say צדקה saves from death?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out two פסוקים in משלי that both say 'צדקה saves from death' and asks why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן raised a difficulty. One פסוק says: 'Wealth will not help on the day of anger, but צדקה saves from death.' Another פסוק says: 'Treasures of wickedness will not help, but צדקה saves from death.' Why do we need these two mentions of צדקה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן notices that the same words appear twice in משלי. He asks why the פסוקים would repeat themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים don't really argue with each other; the problem is that they seem to say the same thing. Since nothing in the פסוקים is extra, each one must teach something different.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a difficulty, sets two sources against each other

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the word is רמי ('raises a contradiction'), the two פסוקים don't disagree. The question is only why the same idea is said twice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yochanan raised a difficulty:
It is written: 'Wealth will not help on the day of anger,
but צדקה saves from death,'
phrases.notes: משלי 11:4

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Treasures of wickedness will not help,
but צדקה saves from death.'
phrases.notes: משלי 10:2

phrases.english: Why are these two mentions of צדקה needed?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 19's idea that צדקה saves from death, now looking at the פסוקים that say it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים in משלי that both say 'וצדקה תציל ממות.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two identical statements seem repetitive, so one of them seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two kinds of saving: from unusual death and from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק teaches that צדקה saves from an unusual death, and the other that it saves from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: One saves him from an unusual death, and one saves him from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: each פסוק teaches a different kind of 'death' that צדקה protects from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition is explained by giving each פסוק its own meaning. One is about this world (a strange, unnatural death), and one is about after death (being judged in גיהנם).

phrases.english: One is that it saves him from an unusual death,
and one is that it saves him from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת שֶׁמַּצִּילָתוֹ מִמִּיתָה מְשׁוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each repeated פסוק a different meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to say the exact same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק is about unusual death in this world, the other about the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.title: Which פסוק is about גיהנם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two פסוקים is the one about being saved from גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is the one that saves him from the judgment of גיהנם?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know there are two meanings, the גמרא asks which meaning goes with which פסוק. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying there are two meanings is not enough; we need a reason from the words of each פסוק to match them up.

phrases.english: And which one is it that saves him
from the judgment of גיהנם?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵי זוֹ הִיא שֶׁמַּצִּילָתוֹ מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to match the answer of step 26 to the פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches being saved from the judgment of גיהנם.

steps.title: The פסוק with 'day of anger' is about גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק that mentions עברה (anger) is about גיהנם, because the Day of Judgment is called a 'day of anger.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the one where 'anger' is written, as it says: 'That day is a day of anger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the פסוק that says 'day of anger' is the one about גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from a פסוק in צפניה that calls the great Day of Judgment a 'day of anger.' So 'יום עברה' in משלי means the day of final judgment, which connects to גיהנם.

keyTerms.meaning: That day, the Day of Judgment

phrases.english: It is the one in which 'anger' is written,
as it is written: 'That day is a day of anger.'
phrases.notes: צפניה 1:15

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ ״עֶבְרָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in משלי 11:4, which mentions 'יום עברה,' refers to the Day of Judgment and saving from גיהנם.

steps.title: Which צדקה saves from an unusual death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks which kind of צדקה is the one that saves from an unusual death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which one is it that saves him from an unusual death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the second meaning. This is a setup line; the answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After matching the גיהנם meaning to one פסוק, the other meaning is left. The גמרא opens the question of what kind of צדקה brings this protection from unusual death.
steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים say 'צדקה saves from death': one means from an unusual death, and the one with 'day of anger' means from the judgment of גיהנם.

phrases.english: And which one is it that saves him
from an unusual death?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵי זוֹ הִיא שֶׁמַּצִּילָתוֹ מִמִּיתָה מְשׁוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the matching question about the second meaning from step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of צדקה saves from an unusual death.
